- Then MSc in Statistics at PUC Chile — ranked 2nd in cohort, GPA 3.75/4.0. Thesis on multinomial logit models. Modules in Bayesian Statistics, Time Series, GLMs, ML Applications.
- Currently at UCL doing MSc AI for Sustainable Development — modules in Probabilistic Modelling, Deep Representations and Learning.
- For the dissertation: exploring Deep Kernel Learning (DKL) — combines deep neural networks with Gaussian Process priors. Interested in the trade-offs of uncertainty quantification.
- Actively studying from GP Summer School (gpss.cc) to deepen understanding of kernel methods.

::: {.notes}
- Key message: I don't just study what I'm told — I actively seek and create research opportunities.
- Dissertation story: I identified the gap between structural risk (Galasso's domain) and probabilistic ML (Guedj's domain). I approached both professors independently and proposed the project that became my dissertation.
- Henry Moss's talk was about how we need constraints and structure in the optimisation of generative models — not just scaling. This resonated with my interest in interpretability.
- Daniel Giles is a PhD student I connected with at these events — building my research network.
- Max Harris collaboration on next-token generation was a lecture project for Knowledge Management and Education module.
- The Oxford professor quote captures why I care about GPs: we need models where we understand what the components mean, not just models that predict well.
- Compositional kernels and GPs are not just a tool for me — they are a core research interest directly aligned with this role.
:::

```{=html}
<div id="kernel-animation" style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.6em; min-height: 60px;">
  <p id="kernel-eq" style="color: #63b3ed; font-family: 'Inter', monospace; font-size: 0.7em; letter-spacing: 0.02em;"></p>
</div>

<div style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.3em;">
  <p style="color: #cbd5e1; font-size: 0.7em;">
    <strong style="color: #63b3ed;">daniel.mardini.25@ucl.ac.uk</strong>
    &nbsp;&bull;&nbsp; <a href="https://danielhuencho.com" style="color: #90cdf4;">danielhuencho.com</a>
    &nbsp;&bull;&nbsp; <a href="https://github.com/choka30" style="color: #90cdf4;">github.com/choka30</a>
  </p>
</div>

<script>
// Kernel equation typing animation
(function() {
  const components = [
    { text: "k_trend", color: "#63b3ed" },
    { text: "k_annual", color: "#90cdf4" },
    { text: "k_weekly", color: "#bee3f8" },
    { text: "k_weather", color: "#63b3ed" },
    { text: "k_calendar", color: "#90cdf4" },
    { text: "k_events", color: "#bee3f8" }
  ];

  const el = document.getElementById('kernel-eq');
  if (!el) return;

  function buildEquation() {
    el.innerHTML = '';
    let prefix = document.createElement('span');
    prefix.style.color = '#94a3b8';
    prefix.textContent = 'k_total = ';
    el.appendChild(prefix);

    let i = 0;
    function addComponent() {
      if (i >= components.length) {
        // Add noise term
        setTimeout(() => {
          let noise = document.createElement('span');
          noise.style.color = '#94a3b8';
          noise.style.opacity = '0';
          noise.style.transition = 'opacity 0.4s ease';
          noise.textContent = ' + \u03B5';
          el.appendChild(noise);
          requestAnimationFrame(() => noise.style.opacity = '1');
        }, 300);
        return;
      }

      if (i > 0) {
        let plus = document.createElement('span');
        plus.style.color = '#4a5568';
        plus.textContent = ' + ';
        el.appendChild(plus);
      }

      let span = document.createElement('span');
      span.style.color = components[i].color;
      span.style.opacity = '0';
      span.style.transform = 'translateY(8px)';
      span.style.display = 'inline-block';
      span.style.transition = 'opacity 0.4s ease, transform 0.4s ease';
      span.style.fontWeight = '600';
      span.textContent = components[i].text;
      el.appendChild(span);

      requestAnimationFrame(() => {
        span.style.opacity = '1';
        span.style.transform = 'translateY(0)';
      });

      i++;
      setTimeout(addComponent, 350);
    }

    setTimeout(addComponent, 200);
  }

  // Run animation when this slide becomes active
  const observer = new MutationObserver(() => {
    const slide = el.closest('section');
    if (slide && slide.classList.contains('present')) {
      buildEquation();
      observer.disconnect();
    }
  });

  // Observe the reveal slides container
  const target = document.querySelector('.reveal .slides');
  if (target) {
    observer.observe(target, { attributes: true, subtree: true, attributeFilter: ['class'] });
  }

  // Also run if already on this slide
  setTimeout(() => {
    const slide = el.closest('section');
    if (slide && slide.classList.contains('present')) {
      buildEquation();
    }
  }, 500);
})();
</script>
```

:::

::: {.notes}
- This slide is the proof. Don't just talk about skills — show the work.
- The UNICON demo is a full compositional GP modelling pipeline on real university energy data (La Trobe University, Australia). This is directly analogous to what the Grand Challenges Living Lab project needs for UCL estates.
- Walk through the 6-component kernel: trend (long-term baseline), annual seasonality (climate-driven), weekly periodicity (occupancy), weather response (nonlinear), calendar effects (academic year), events (interventions like COVID, LED installations).
- 8 building categories modelled independently — enables cross-building comparison of how GPs capture different building physics. This is exactly the "generalisation across locations" the role description asks for.
- Anomaly detection using standardised GP residuals — higher use than expected from similar locations.
- The demo is live at danielhuencho.com — encourage them to explore it.
- Close with contact information and express genuine enthusiasm for the role.
:::
